title: What Darwin Got Wrong

turns.speaker: Rhys Lindmark
turns.text: Evolution itself has evolved over time the ideas of evolution. The idea is called this extended evolutionary synthesis. And this is what I'd say is like the most cutting edge version of evolutionary thought. We start with Darwin, 1860-ish. We have this selection of inherited variation, and he got selection right. The way we get complexity in the world is not through God, but is rather through this unknowing process that selects for increasingly adapted creatures. And so he got the selection part right, the survival of the fittest Malthusian competition. What he didn't know anything about was how variation works or how inheritance works.
